review_comments: [team convention] Round money only with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent). Python's round() and a bare Decimal.quantize() use banker's rounding and give wrong invoice totals.

item.title: Round monetary results with the project's round_money helper
item.description: Any money value returned from a calculation must be passed through ledgerly.money.round_money, not Python round() or bare Decimal.quantize(), because those use banker's rounding.
item.content: Before returning a computed money amount, wrap it in round_money(...) (half-up to the cent). Check the repo's money module for the canonical helper and reuse it rather than inventing rounding logic.

item.title: Read the money module before implementing financial math
item.description: Inspecting ledgerly/money.py early reveals helpers like to_money, round_money, and ZERO that encode team conventions and avoid float pitfalls.
item.content: When a task involves prices or totals, open the money/utility module first and use its conversion and rounding functions (e.g., to_money for inputs, round_money for outputs) instead of raw arithmetic.

item.title: Address reviewer conventions even when tests pass
item.description: Passing the visible test suite does not mean the change is accepted; team-convention comments must be applied explicitly.
item.content: After a review rejection, locate the exact spot the convention applies to (e.g., the return statement) and apply the required helper, then re-run tests and inspect the final code to confirm the change landed.
